newsitem.title: CHINA: Bank of China aims to reduce bad loan ratio.
newsitem.headline: Bank of China aims to reduce bad loan ratio.

text.p: The Bank of China aims to reduce its bad loan ratio by two to three percentage points this year, the China Daily said on Monday.
The bank would reform its credit management and supervision systems this year to cut down on bad loans and financial fraud, the newspaper quoted bank president Wang Xuebin as saying.
He gave no details of the current ratio of bad loans to total credits.
Clearing bad assets should coincide with business expansion, Wang said.
"We will promote the adjustment of assets structure through business development," he said.
The bank had adjusted its credit structure in the last six months, focusing on extending loans to large and medium-sized state firms, he said.

The bank's deposits at the end of June totalled 519 billion yuan ($62.5 billion), up 30 billion yuan from the end of last year, while foreign exchange savings in the first half reached $31.4 billion, it said.
By the end of June, outstanding foreign exchange loans totalled $60.7 billion, accounting for 60 percent of total foreign exchange loans made by China's four state-owned commercial banks, it said.
